description: This map presents satellite imagery of a coastal landscape, likely in Southern Europe, rendered in a false-colour composite. A large dark blue area representing the sea or ocean borders the landmass to the north and east. The land cover on the terrestrial side is predominantly reddish/brownish, which, in this false-colour scheme, represents healthy forest or dense vegetation. These areas are interspersed with lighter yellowish/beige patches, indicative of agricultural fields, scrub, or bare ground. A conspicuous yellow arrow highlights a central area within the forested region that exhibits a distinct greenish to bluish colouration. According to the surrounding documentation, these greenish/bluish hues indicate "other damaged forest," often caused by factors such as bark-beetle infestation, storms, or fires, which lead to visible discolouration in the forest canopy as captured by Earth Observation data. The damaged area appears as a compact feature contrasting sharply with the surrounding healthier red/brown forest. No scale bar, compass, legend, or specific geographic names are visible on the map.
